original_card.question: Is there a genuinely unsearched, explicitly bounded improvement to the selected packing?
methods: Search a named unclaimed canonical candidate domain with a reproducible partition.
Prove a stronger scoped relaxation or exact optimum for one named residual subproblem.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Check live PR overlap first, price both suppliers and distinguish a search best from an optimum.

first_step.inspect: Locate the selected packing source in the review and check live PRs for the same residual problem.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Define an unclaimed canonical domain and a favorable bound before starting a new search.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An actual paid-profile gain can improve the frontier up to the other supplier cap.
allowed_variations: One bounded residual packing instance or exact relaxation.
scope_change_triggers: Rerunning an existing search with only a different seed as a separate mathematical contribution.

actual_scope: Bit-side selected packing: can any nine-stage stage recipe (K = 4 exchanged pairs, one rank-1 local per stage, at most one +-1 bridge before each local, entries |<= 8|) change PR #589's idle windows so that PR #442 whole-residual hosting (width 8, 0 banks, paid remainder <= 45) raises the exact nine-stage bit c above 1733427039589844234749/10^24?
scope_change_reason: The card's starting points are complex-side packings. Here the packing is the selected bit supplier's: 3,951 width-8 residuals per replica in the idle windows of the nine-stage template. research/bit589-width-packing proved that re-hosting cannot help with the template recipe's windows held fixed; this search varies the recipe that generates those windows. The canonical domain is every valid recipe of the stated class, enumerated exhaustively (not a seeded heuristic).
bottleneck_link: Side result for the non-binding supplier: the selected #1094 assembly is complex-bound (complex b 0.0016755 < bit c 0.0017334), so a bit gain only raises the bit cap. It closes the recipe/hosting lever for PR #589's word in this class and leaves helper width (bit589-width-packing) as the identified bit-side lever.
stop_rule: Price the optimistic bound over all idle-segment partitions first; then enumerate the class exhaustively and price every distinct window structure exactly; stop at the first structure above PR #589's c or at completion of the enumeration.
evidence: 2,070,720 valid recipes (1,064 window structures, 9-11 idle segments, max advance 6 levels). Capacity is 27 - #segments <= 18 slots per copy set (3,996 vs 3,951 needed) for every structure; 46 are hostable with 0 banks; the best c equals PR #589's exactly (8 tied structures, identical remainder), none is higher. Template recipe reproduces PR #589's c and frozen selection from the recipe alone; official hosting_k.solve agrees on the top and template structures. The 2K+1 local-count floor (duplicating open #743) is re-proved in PROOF.md. See README.md and EXPECTED.json.

open_questions.question: Can a gap holding several bridges (a Levi element with support larger than two pairs) give a K = 4 recipe with fewer than 9 idle segments or an advance of 7-8 levels?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only route left inside the nine-stage, width-8 template that could raise hosting capacity above 18 slots (the R <= 4v wall) or reach the optimistic +1.04% layouts.
open_questions.first_step: Run recipe_search.py 3 --bridges-per-gap 2 with stronger pruning (the plain run did not finish in 20 minutes on 12 cores) and compare its idle-partition set with the single-bridge one.
open_questions.blocked_by: Search cost; a segment-count proof (next question) would replace it.

open_questions.question: Is 'at least 3(K-1) idle segments' a theorem for every bridge recipe that exchanges K pairs with 2K+1 rank-1 locals?
open_questions.why_it_matters: With floor(7D/8) = D-1 it would make the width-8 hosting wall R <= 4v recipe-independent at every K, closing the recipe lever without enumeration.
open_questions.first_step: Generalise the observed minima (3, 6, 9 segments for K = 2, 3, 4): K-1 entry advances, K-1 final advances, and one level-synchronising advance per borrowing step between pairs.
open_questions.blocked_by: A written proof of the synchronisation count; the rank invariants of PROOF.md bound locals, not level syncs.

open_questions.question: Once width-7 bit helpers exist, which recipe minimises the idle remainder?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Width 7 divides every 7D window, so capacity becomes 27 slots per copy set for every recipe and the recipe ranking may change; bit589-width-packing prices up to +23% for the template alone.
open_questions.first_step: Re-price data/search-K4.json with width-7 residuals (generalise recipe_lib.host to width w) under bit589-width-packing's local-profile bracket.
open_questions.blocked_by: No width-7 bit helper exists yet (H4 literal cleanup retiming, per bit589-width-packing).
